findings.title: FileReader lifecycle gap in useImportHandlers.ts — no abort on unmount
findings.why_it_matters: Resolved this loop. FileReader onload fires after unmount, dispatching stale state updates.
findings.what_is_wrong: useImportHandlers.ts prior to this loop: FileReader created inline inside useCallback with no ref; no useEffect cleanup; pending read cannot be aborted on unmount or on second call.
findings.leverage_impact: Hook Interface now owns lifecycle safety; callers need not manage FileReader lifetime.
findings.locality_impact: Abort logic concentrated inside the hook where it belongs.
findings.why_weakens_submission: Unmounted component dispatch is a React concurrency hazard; now resolved.
findings.minimal_correction_path: Store reader in useRef<FileReader | null>; add useEffect cleanup calling readerRef.current?.abort(); abort previous reader at top of onImportFile.

builder_notes.pattern: FileReader created inline with no ref = orphaned read
builder_notes.how_to_recognize: const reader = new FileReader() inside a useCallback with no useRef storing it
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: If you create a reader/socket inside useCallback, store it in useRef and abort it in useEffect cleanup.
builder_notes.stack_example: useImportHandlers.ts: readerRef = useRef<FileReader | null>(null); useEffect(() => () => readerRef.current?.abort(), [])

builder_notes.pattern: Abort before start — second call must cancel the first
builder_notes.how_to_recognize: readAsText called without first checking readerRef.current for a pending read
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: At top of onImportFile: readerRef.current?.abort() before new FileReader().

builder_notes.pattern: Mock must include abort — happy-path mock breaks on unmount cleanup
builder_notes.how_to_recognize: Tests pass in isolation but fail on cleanup with 'abort is not a function'
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: Add abort: jest.fn() to every FileReader mock.
builder_notes.stack_example: useImportHandlers.test.ts mockFileReaderWith — added abort: jest.fn() to fix cleanup failure.
